heading: BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY
translated_text:
BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

REGENT OF NORTH CENTRAL TIMOR

PROVINCE OF EAST NUSA TENGGARA

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF NORTH CENTRAL TIMOR REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is North Central Timor Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of North Central Timor Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of North Central Timor.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of North Central Timor Regency.
5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of North Central Timor Regency.
6. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and Child Protection.
7. Head of Agency is the Head of Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.
8. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus in North Central Timor Regency. 9. Head of Regional Apparatus is the Head of Regional Apparatus in North Central Timor Regency.
10. Board is a Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of development planning and regional research.
11. Head of Board is a Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of planning.
12. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
13. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development policies and programs.
14. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of social construction and can change due to social and cultural circumstances of society.
15. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in the development process.
16. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and women.
17. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG, is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.
18. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point, hereinafter referred to as Focal Point PUG, is a PD apparatus that has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
19. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD, is an elaboration of the vision, mission and programs of the Regent whose preparation is guided by the Regional Long-Term Development Plan, which contains regional development strategies, general regional policies, 3 regional programs and a macroeconomic framework that includes an overview of the economy as a whole including the direction of fiscal policy in a work plan in the form of a regulatory framework and a funding framework that is indicative.
20. Gender Analysis is a process built systematically to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in development and the benefits they enjoy.
21. Gender Responsive Budget is a performance-based budget allocation for certain programs or activities whose input, output, and outcome indicators can ensure the fulfillment of the aspirations and needs of women and men fairly.
22. Communication, Information and Education, hereinafter abbreviated as KIE, is the delivery of messages in the form of information, ideas or facts related to gender mainstreaming that need to be known by the public directly or indirectly through communication channels to message recipients to obtain effects, as a process of behavioral change towards gender responsiveness.
23. Village/Sub-district Development Planning Deliberation, hereinafter referred to as Musrembangkel, is an annual village/sub-district development planning deliberation forum that involves development actors in the Village/Sub-district.
24. District Development Planning Deliberation, hereinafter referred to as Musrembangcam, is a deliberation forum among development actors to discuss and agree on steps to handle priority program activities listed in the list of proposed village development planning activities that are integrated with the development priorities of the North Central Timor Regency in the district area coordinated by the Regional Development Planning Board and implemented by the District Head.
25. Development planning deliberation for the preparation of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter referred to as Musrembang RPJMD, is a deliberation forum among stakeholders to discuss, sharpen and agree on the draft Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
26. Strategic Plan, hereinafter referred to as Renstra, is a five-year planning document that contains the vision, mission, objectives, strategies, policies, programs and development activities in accordance with the organizational tasks and functions as an elaboration of the RPJMD.
27. Work Plan, hereinafter referred to as Renja, is a one-year planning document that contains development policies, programs, and activities both planned directly by the Regional Apparatus and pursued by encouraging community participation as an elaboration of the Renstra.
28. Regional Government Work Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RKPD, is a one-year planning document that contains development policies, programs, and activities both planned directly by the Regional Government and pursued by encouraging community participation as an elaboration of the Renstra.
29. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is an activity planning document prepared by a technical team to be implemented in a certain period/time.
30. Gender Analysis Pathway, hereinafter abbreviated as GAP, is a gender analysis tool that can be used to assist planners in mainstreaming gender in planning development policies/programs/activities with the aim of identifying gender gaps and gender issues as well as simultaneously preparing policy/program/activity plans aimed at reducing or eliminating such gender gaps.
31. Technical Team is a Team formed by Pokja PUG with the task of conducting gender-perspective budget analysis and preparing the PUG RAD.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

SCOPE

Article 2

The scope of Women's Empowerment implementation includes:
a. quality of life of women;
b. protection of women;
c. quality of family; and
d. gender data system.

heading: CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

QUALITY OF LIFE OF WOMEN

Part One

General

heading: Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

Quality of Life of Women includes:
a. institutionalization of PUG;
b. Women's Empowerment in the political, legal, social and economic fields in community organizations; and
c. strengthening and development of women's empowerment service provider institutions.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Institutionalization of PUG Paragraph General

heading: Article 4
Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Coordinator

heading: Article 5
translated_text:
Article 5

1. The Regent has the authority to appoint the Head of PD who administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment as the coordinator of PUG implementation.
2. The appointment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be by Regent's Decree.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Pokja PUG

heading: Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

1. The Regent has the authority to establish the PUG Working Group.
2. The establishment of the PUG Working Group as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.
3. The Regent's Decree as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be valid for 5 (five) years.
4. The management of the PUG Working Group consists of:
a. chairperson by the head of agency;
b. secretariat by the head of service;
c. members including:
1\. head of PD;
2\. technical team consisting of:
a. apparatus who have attended training or education in gender-responsive budget analysis of at most 5 (five) persons.
b. representatives of university elements of at most 5 (five) persons;
c. press representatives of at most 5 (five) persons; and
d. representatives of non-governmental organizations having scope of orientation in the field of gender of at most 5 (five) persons.

heading: Article 7
Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

PUG Focal Point

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

1. The Regional Secretary has the authority to establish a PUG Focal Point within the Regional Secretariat.
2. The establishment of the PUG Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regional Secretary's Decree.
3. The management of the PUG Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. person in charge by the regional secretary;
b. coordinator by echelon IIB official in charge of governmental affairs in the field of law;
c. vice coordinator by echelon IIIA official of each division in the regional secretariat except for echelon IIB official as referred to in letter b; and
d. members by representatives of officials and/or staff from all divisions in the regional secretariat.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. The Head of PD is obliged to establish a PD PUG Focal Point.
2. The establishment of the PUG Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) by Head of PD's Decree.
3. The management of the PUG Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. person in charge by the head of PD;
b. coordinator by echelon III A official in charge of planning affairs at the PD;
c. Vice Coordinator by Echelon IIIB Official who has competence in PUG; and
d. Members by representatives of Officials or staff from divisions and secretariat at the PD.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. The Hospital Director has the authority to establish a Hospital PUG Focal Point.
2. The establishment of the PUG Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Hospital Director's decree.
3. The management of the PUG Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. person in charge by the hospital director;
b. coordinator by echelon IIIB official in charge of hospital planning;
c. vice coordinator by echelon IVA official who has competence in PUG; and
d. members by representatives of officials or staff in divisions or sections existing in the hospital.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

1. The Head of the Community Health Center has the authority to establish a Puskesmas PUG Focal Point.
2. The establishment of the PUG Focal Point as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Head of Community Health Center's Decree.
3. The management of the puskesmas PUG Focal Point consists of:
a. person in charge by the Head of Puskesmas;
b. coordinator by echelon IV B official in charge of Puskesmas planning; and
c. members consisting of Puskesmas staff.

heading: Article 12
Paragraph 5
translated_text:
Paragraph 5

Gender-based Regional Development Planning

heading: Article 13
Article 14
Article 15
Paragraph 6
translated_text:
Paragraph 6

Budgeting

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

1. Regional Government is obliged to allocate budget for the implementation of PUG in the Region.
2. Implementation budget as referred to in paragraph (1) is sourced from:
a. APBD; and
b. assistance from other parties that is not binding, as long as it is in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.
3. Budget as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), is used to finance the activities of Pokja PUG and Focal Point PUG PD in integrating Gender at the level of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies and development in the Region.

heading: Paragraph 7
translated_text:
Paragraph 7

Monitoring and Evaluation

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

1. The Regent is authorized to conduct monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of PUG.
2. The Regent may delegate the implementation of monitoring and evaluation to Pokja PUG.
3. Monitoring and evaluation is conducted at each PD and/or other institutions that carry out PUG efforts.
4. Monitoring and evaluation is implemented at least once every 6 (six) months.

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

Monitoring of PUG implementation is conducted through:
a. monitoring the preparation of gender responsive development planning documents both at the PD level and at the regional level;
b. monitoring RAD PUG; and
c. verification of RAD PUG implementation Reports.

heading: Article 19
Paragraph 8
translated_text:
Paragraph 8

PUG Reporting

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. Pokja PUG is responsible for preparing PUG Implementation Report every 6 (six) months and RAD PUG Implementation Report every five years.
2. Reporting framework as referred to in paragraph (1) is guided by the reporting framework as referred to in laws and regulations concerning General Guidelines for PUG Implementation in Regions.
3. Pokja PUG Report as referred to in paragraph (1) is reported to the Regent.
4. The Regent is responsible for examining and declaring approval of Pokja PUG Report as referred to in paragraph (1).
5. The Regent is responsible for sending pokja PUG report as referred to in paragraph (1) to the Minister who administers Home Affairs governmental affairs.

heading: Paragraph 9
translated_text:
Paragraph 9

Supervision

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. The Regent is responsible for conducting supervision of PUG implementation.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of:
a. Gender responsive planning and budgeting conducted by the regional government budget team;
b. implementation of coordination between Pokja PUG and Focal Point gender; and
c. progress of RAD PUG achievement every year.
3. Responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) technically and operationally may be carried out by the Chairperson of Pokja PUG and the Head of Pokja PUG Secretariat.
4. Implementation of responsibility as referred to in paragraph (3) is reported to the Regent.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Women's Empowerment in the Fields of Politics, Law, Social Culture and Economy in Community Organizations

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

General

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

Women's Empowerment efforts in the fields of politics, law, social culture and economy in community organizations include stages:
a. planning;
b. implementation; and
c. reporting and evaluation.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Planning

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. The Agency is responsible for facilitating the planning of Women's Empowerment in the fields of politics, law, social culture and economy in community organizations.
2. Planning as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted in an integrated manner in development planning deliberations based on gender analysis pathway instruments.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Implementation

heading: Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

Implementation of Women's Empowerment in community organizations is carried out by PD in accordance with the main duties and functions carried out in accordance with regional financial capacity.

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

1. PD that administers governmental affairs in the field of national unity and politics is responsible for facilitating women's empowerment in the field of politics.
2. Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. conducting education and training for women in order to improve competence especially in the field of politics; and
b. encouraging the representation of women in every management of community organizations.

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. PD that administers governmental affairs in the field of law is responsible for facilitating Women's Empowerment in the field of law.
2. Implementation of Women's Empowerment in the field of law includes:
a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the field of law through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. PD that administers governmental affairs in the social field is responsible for facilitating Women's Empowerment in the field of social culture.
2. Women's Empowerment in the field of social culture through:
a. increasing knowledge, attitudes and skills to encourage the fulfillment of tiered education in accordance with potential to improve social status;
b. increasing awareness, willingness and ability to overcome health problems through quality promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts especially in the field of reproductive health;
c. increasing awareness and knowledge about independent, healthy and prosperous family planning including access to consultation services and marriage registration; and
d. facilitation and efforts to preserve customs and development of science, technology, arts and culture for the advancement of women.

heading: Article 28
Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Reporting and Evaluation

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. Each PD is responsible for making a report on the implementation of Women's Empowerment activities that have been carried out to the Regent through the Office.
2. The Office after receiving the report submitted by PD conducts an evaluation of the implementation of activities.
3. Results of evaluation of implementation of activities as referred to in paragraph (2) are reported to the Regent.
4. Results of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (3) are used for budgeting planning for the following year.

heading: CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Part One

General

heading: Article 30
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Strengthening And Development Of Women's Protection Service Provider Institutions

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Children Protection

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

1. PD that administers governmental affairs in the field of institutions and organizations is responsible for facilitating the formation of regional technical implementation unit for women and children protection.
2. Formation of UPTD P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is regulated by Regent Regulation.
3. Formation of UPTD P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (2) at the latest 2 (two) years after this Regional Regulation is stipulated.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Regional Action Plan

heading: Article 32
Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Monitoring and Evaluation

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

1. The Regent shall monitor the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women.
2. The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of women in the Region.
3. The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted periodically on Regional Apparatus through the Agency.
4. Monitoring shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of women for the current year.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of women shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women for the following year.
3. The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Prevention of Violence Against Women

heading: Article 35
Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Strengthening and Development of Service Provider Institutions for the Protection of Women Victims of Violence

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. The Agency may provide assistance to Service Institutions located in the region in the form of:
a. strengthening of Service Institutions; and
b. development of Service Institutions.
2. Strengthening of service institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be implemented through:
a. improving the competence of service institution members; and/or
b. facilitating paralegal training on a regular basis.
3. Development of Service Institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented through:
a. providing additional facilities and infrastructure;
b. providing information technology-based service approaches; and/or
c. recruiting village cadres as paralegal assistants.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

FAMILY QUALITY

Part One

General

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

Family Quality includes:
a. improving family quality in realizing gender equality; and
b. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for improving family quality in realizing gender equality.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Improving Family Quality in Realizing Gender Equality

heading: Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

1. The Agency is responsible for facilitating family quality improvement activities in the Region.
2. Improving family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented through:
a. facilitating the establishment of service provider institutions;
b. in coordination with Regional Apparatus and/or related institutions that have the main tasks and functions to carry out activities:
1\. improving entrepreneurial skills for women; or
2\. developing job training for women.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Strengthening And Development of Service Provider Institutions for Improving Family Quality in Realizing Gender Equality

heading: Article 39
CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

GENDER DATA SYSTEM

Part One

General

heading: Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

Gender Data System includes:
a. data collection;
b. data processing; and
c. analysis and presentation of gender data.

Part Two Data Collection

heading: Article 41
translated_text:
Article 41

1. Regional Apparatus that carries out the duties of PUG focal point is responsible for reporting Gender data and PUG activities implemented to the Regent through the Agency.
2. Reporting of Gender data and PUG activities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted every 6 (six) months.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Data Processing

heading: Article 42
translated_text:
Article 42

1. The Agency after receiving reports of Gender data and PUG activities from each Gender focal point in the region shall conduct data processing.
2. Data processing as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented to sort Gender data and PUG activities with good grouping and easy to analyze.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Analysis And Presentation of Gender Data

heading: Article 43
translated_text:
Article 43

1. The Agency shall conduct analysis of the processed data.
2. The analysis as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented comprehensively based on adequate mapping so that it is easy to understand.
3. The adequate analysis as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be presented as regional Gender data manually and/or electronically.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 44

Regional Apparatus that do not establish PUG Focal Points as referred to in Article 8, Article 9, Article 10 and Article 11 shall be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. verbal warning;
b. written warning; or
c. statement of dissatisfaction.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 45

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, existing service provider institutions for the protection of women shall continue to carry out their duties until the establishment of regional technical implementing units for the protection of women and children in accordance with the provisions of this Regional Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 46

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of North Central Timor Regency.

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF NORTH CENTRAL TIMOR REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF NORTH CENTRAL TIMOR REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2020 CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF NORTH CENTRAL TIMOR REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their task is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be opposed, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding of the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.
